For adults, the lowest deductible is 300 francs and the highest 2500 francs.
For children, the deductible is 0 francs as standard.
The higher the chosen deductible, the lower the monthly premium.
After the deductible you also pay an excess of 10 per cent.
The deductible starts again from the beginning every year on 1 January.
You can change the amount of the deductible with effect from the start of the next year.

abschnitte.text: The **deductible** is a form of cost sharing in compulsory **basic insurance**. It is set out in the Health Insurance Act (KVG). If you receive a doctor’s bill, you pay it yourself until your costs for the year reach the amount of the deductible. Only after that does the health insurer cover most of the costs. The deductible applies per person and per calendar year.

Adults from 19 can choose between six levels: 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500 francs. The **standard deductible** of 300 francs is the lowest. For children up to 18, the deductible is 0 francs as standard. But parents can also take an **optional deductible** of 100 to 600 francs for their children. They then get a discount on the premium for this.

Anyone who chooses a high deductible gets a **premium discount**. With a deductible of 2500 francs you can save up to around 1500 francs a year in premiums, because the discount is limited by law. But if you fall ill, you first have to pay the whole 2500 francs yourself. For healthy people who rarely go to the doctor, a high deductible is often worth it. Anyone who is chronically ill or needs medicines regularly is usually better off with 300 francs.

Anna has a deductible of 300 francs and doctor’s bills of 1300 francs in the year. First she pays the 300-franc deductible herself. Of the remaining 1000 francs, she pays 10 per cent as the **excess**, in other words 100 francs. Altogether Anna bears 400 francs, and the health insurer covers 900 francs. On top of that, Anna of course pays her premium every month.

The deductible can be changed with effect from 1 January each year. Anyone who wants to lower the deductible usually has to tell the health insurer by the end of November. Raising it is usually still possible until 31 December. Anyone who expects high costs in the next year, for example because of a planned **operation**, should switch to 300 francs in good time. Some services are exempt from the deductible, for example maternity services.

begriffe.erklaerung: Amount you pay yourself each year before the health insurer covers costs.
Amount you pay to the health insurer every month.
10 per cent of the costs that you still bear yourself after the deductible, up to an upper limit.
Compulsory health insurance that everyone living in Switzerland must have.

gewusst: When the KVG was introduced in 1996, the lowest deductible was still 150 francs.
No deductible has to be paid for services connected with pregnancy and birth.
Many young and healthy adults choose the highest deductible of 2500 francs to save on premiums.

teile.einleitung: A plaster is a small dressing that sticks on. It protects small wounds from dirt so that they can heal well. That is why plasters in different sizes belong in every home first aid kit.
wichtigste: A plaster protects small wounds from dirt.
First you clean the wound, then the plaster goes on.
The plaster has a soft wound pad and a sticky strip.
Large, deep or heavily bleeding wounds need to be seen by a doctor.
Plasters belong in every home first aid kit.

abschnitte.text: A **plaster** is a small dressing that sticks on. In the middle it has a soft **wound pad**, which soaks up blood and does not stick to the wound. All around it, a **sticky strip** holds the plaster on the skin. There are plasters in many sizes and shapes. For the heel, for example, there are special **blister plasters**.

If you have grazed your knee, first **clean** the wound. Rinse away dirt and small stones with clean water. Then you can **disinfect** the wound. Only then does the **plaster** go on. It protects the wound from new dirt so that it can heal well.

A plaster is only enough for **small wounds**. If a wound is large or deep or is bleeding heavily, go to the doctor. This also applies if dirt will not come out or if an animal has bitten you. Protection against **tetanus**, a dangerous infection, is also important. There is a vaccination against it.

gewusst: Sticking plasters with a wound pad, as we know them today, came onto the market in the 1920s.

teile.einleitung: The health insurer helps to pay the costs when someone falls ill. In Switzerland, every person who lives here must have basic insurance, right from birth.
wichtigste: In Switzerland, basic insurance is compulsory for everyone.
Babies and children must be insured too.
For children, the parents usually take out the health insurance and pay for it.
The health insurer pays, for example, for visits to the doctor, medicines and hospital.
You pay a premium for this every month.
The Confederation supervises health insurers through the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH).

abschnitte.text: A health insurer works like a large community. All insured people pay an amount every month, the **premium**. This money pays for the treatment of those who fall ill. A stay in hospital can be very expensive. Thanks to health insurance, nobody has to pay for expensive treatment entirely on their own.

Since 1996, the **Health Insurance Act** has applied in Switzerland. It states that every person who lives in Switzerland must have **basic insurance**. This applies even to **babies**. For children, the parents take out the insurance and usually pay for it too. You can choose your health insurer freely.

Basic insurance pays costs connected with **illness**: visits to the doctor, many medicines, treatment in hospital and much more. Exactly what is included is set out by law. That is why the services are the same at all insurers. For extras such as a single room in hospital, there is voluntary **supplementary insurance**. No health insurer pays for toys or sweets.

Health insurers have to stick to the rules. The **Confederation** watches over this, and the **Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH)** is responsible. It checks the premiums every year, for example. The **cantons** help people on a small income with premium reductions.

gewusst: In Switzerland there are several dozen health insurers that offer basic insurance.
The premium depends on age, where you live, the deductible and the model you have chosen.

teile.einleitung: Health insurance helps to pay the costs when someone falls ill or has an accident. Many people regularly pay a contribution into a shared pot. The bills of those who need help are then paid out of this pot.
wichtigste: Health insurance covers costs for the doctor, hospital and medicines.
It works on the principle of solidarity: healthy people help pay for those who are ill.
Insured people pay contributions for it, which in Switzerland are called premiums.
In Switzerland, the health insurer helps to pay these costs.
In 1883, Germany was the first country to introduce statutory health insurance for workers.
The countries of the world organise their health insurance in very different ways.
In Switzerland, basic insurance is compulsory for everyone.

abschnitte.text: A serious illness or an operation can cost tens of thousands of francs. Many families could not pay that on their own. That is why many people join together and share the **risk**. Everyone pays a smaller amount, and anyone who falls ill gets help from the shared money. This principle is called **solidarity**.

Even in the Middle Ages, guilds and brotherhoods had funds that helped members who were ill. In the 19th century, workers in many places founded their own **relief funds**. In 1883, the German Chancellor Otto von Bismarck introduced the first statutory health insurance for workers. In Switzerland, the people approved the Health and Accident Insurance Act in 1912. However, basic insurance only became compulsory for everyone in Switzerland in 1996.

Around the world there are two well-known basic models. In the **Bismarck model**, employees and employers pay contributions to health insurers, as in Germany, for example. In the **Beveridge model**, the health system is paid for through taxes, as with the National Health Service in Great Britain since 1948. Switzerland has its own system with per-person premiums that each individual pays. In the USA, many people are insured through their employer.

Typically, health insurance covers visits to the doctor, hospital stays and prescribed **medicines**. Tests such as X-rays or blood tests are also included. Often you have to bear part of the costs yourself. This is meant to encourage people not to use the health system unnecessarily. Exactly what is paid for is set out by law in each country.

In Switzerland, the insurers are called **health insurance funds** (Krankenkassen). There are about 40 of them (as of 2025), including large ones such as CSS, Helsana or Swica. They all offer the same basic insurance, but the premiums differ. There is also voluntary **supplementary insurance**, for example for braces or a single room in hospital. Health insurers are supervised by the Federal Office of Public Health (FOPH).

begriffe.erklaerung: Regular contribution that you pay to the health insurer.
People who are registered with an insurer.
Standing together: many people jointly help those who need help.
The possibility that something bad or expensive will happen.

gewusst: Switzerland spends as much money per person on health as only a few other countries in the world.
The German word “Kasse” recalls the old relief funds, into which members used to pay money together.

teile.einleitung: Tax fraud is a serious way of not paying taxes correctly. It involves using forged or false documents, for example a changed salary statement. Tax fraud is punished by a criminal court.
wichtigste: Tax fraud involves using forged or false documents.
A document might be, for example, a salary statement or a set of accounts.
Tax fraud is an offence and is judged by a criminal court.
It can lead to a fine or a prison sentence.
In addition, you have to pay the missing taxes.
Without forgery, it is called tax evasion.

abschnitte.text: Anyone who wants to save tax and **forges a document** to do so is committing **tax fraud**. A document here is something that is meant to prove something, such as a salary statement, an invoice or a balance sheet. If such a document is changed or created with false content and shown to the tax office, that is fraud. An example: Tim changes his salary statement and writes in a lower wage.

In **tax evasion**, someone keeps quiet about income or wealth but does not forge anything. It is punished with a fine. In **tax fraud**, forgery is added. That is why it counts as an **offence** and goes before the **criminal court**. In short: forging turns evasion into fraud.

Anyone who commits tax fraud has to pay the taxes they underpaid as **back taxes** with interest. On top of that there is usually a fine for the evasion. The criminal court can also impose a **monetary penalty** or a **prison sentence**. Tax fraud is unfair, because then everyone else has to bear more.

gewusst: For tax fraud involving direct federal tax, the penalty can be up to three years in prison or a monetary penalty.

teile.einleitung: The eyes are an important sense organ. If you cannot see well or your eyes hurt, the eye doctor can help. She checks how well you can see and finds out whether you might need glasses.
wichtigste: Eye doctors are experts on the eyes.
The specialist field is called **eye medicine** or ophthalmology.
In an eye test you read letters or symbols on a chart.
People who cannot see well often get glasses or contact lenses.
Eye doctors also treat diseases and injuries of the eyes.
A medical examination is needed for health insurance to contribute to children’s glasses.

abschnitte.text: Light enters the eye through the **cornea** and the **pupil**. The **lens** focuses the light like a magnifying glass. At the back of the eye is the **retina**. It turns the light into signals that travel along the optic nerve to the brain. Only the brain turns them into a picture.

In an eye test you look at a chart with letters, numbers or symbols that get smaller and smaller. Each eye is tested separately. The eye doctor can also look into the eye with instruments. Sometimes you are given drops to make the pupil bigger. Afterwards you see a bit blurry for a while, but that wears off again.

People who are **short-sighted** see near things clearly but distant things blurred. People who are **long-sighted** tend to have trouble with things that are close. With **astigmatism**, you see things distorted. Glasses or contact lenses correct these problems. Then you can see clearly again, for example the board at school.

The **eye doctor** has studied medicine. She examines the eyes, recognises diseases and can prescribe medicines or operate. The **optician** is an expert in glasses and contact lenses. He measures how strong your eyesight is and fits the glasses. For children, you usually go to the eye doctor or the paediatrician first.

In Switzerland, the examination for an eye disease is paid for by the **basic insurance** of the health insurance fund, after the deductible and the excess. It pays a contribution towards children’s glasses if a doctor has prescribed them. That is why you have your eyes examined first.

gewusst: The image on the retina is actually upside down. Only the brain turns it the right way round.
We blink many times a minute. This keeps the eyes moist and clean.

teile.einleitung: Wealth tax is a tax on what you own, for example savings, shares or a house. In Switzerland it is collected by the cantons and municipalities, and the Confederation does not charge one. Switzerland is one of the few countries in Europe that still has such a tax.
wichtigste: Wealth tax is charged on what a person owns.
In Switzerland, the cantons and municipalities collect a wealth tax.
The Confederation does not collect a wealth tax.
What counts is wealth on 31 December minus debts.
Small amounts of wealth are tax-free thanks to tax-free allowances.
The tax rates are usually only a few per mille.
Companies also pay a similar tax on their equity.

abschnitte.text: **Wealth** includes everything you own that is worth money. This includes money in accounts, shares, funds, houses, flats, cars or valuable jewellery. With **wealth tax** you pay a small part of it to the state every year. You may subtract debts, for example a mortgage, from your wealth.

In Switzerland, wealth tax is a matter for the cantons and **municipalities**. The Confederation has no right to collect such a tax. Each canton sets its own rates and **tax-free allowances**. That is why the tax varies a lot depending on where you live.

The rates are usually given in **per mille**, in other words in thousandths. At a rate of 3 per mille, you pay 300 francs a year on wealth of 100,000 francs. In most cantons wealth tax is also progressive, so large fortunes are taxed more heavily. Small savings remain completely tax-free thanks to tax-free allowances.

You declare your wealth in the tax return, with the amount as of 31 December. For bank balances and securities you fill in the **list of securities**. Houses and flats are not counted at their market price, but at an officially set tax value. These values are often lower than the price you would get if you sold them.

Many European countries have abolished wealth tax; Germany, for example, has not collected it since 1997. In Switzerland it brings the cantons and municipalities several billion francs every year. Supporters say that this way rich people make a fair contribution. Critics think that wealth is taxed twice as a result, because it often comes from income on which tax has already been paid.

begriffe.erklaerung: Everything you own that is worth money, minus debts.
One thousandth, in other words 0.1 per cent.
Amount on which you do not have to pay any tax.
Part of the tax return with all accounts and securities.

gewusst: Children can also have wealth, but until they come of age it is taxed with their parents.
Switzerland is one of only a few countries in Europe that still has a general wealth tax.
A house counts as wealth, even if you live in it yourself.

teile.einleitung: In summer, bees, wasps or mosquitoes sometimes sting or bite. Usually a sting is harmless and only burns for a while, but in rare cases quick help is needed.
wichtigste: Bees, wasps and mosquitoes can sting or bite.
Cooling relieves pain and swelling.
With a bee, the sting often stays stuck in the skin.
Anyone who has trouble breathing after a sting needs help immediately via 144.
A sting in the mouth or throat is an emergency.

abschnitte.text: **Bees** and **wasps** sting to defend themselves. With a bee, the barbed sting often stays stuck in the skin. You remove it carefully by pushing it sideways with your fingernail. Wasps can sting several times. **Mosquitoes**, on the other hand, bite to suck blood and leave an itchy spot.

To ease the burning, it helps to **cool** the spot, for example with a cold flannel or an ice pack wrapped in a cloth. This relieves the pain and the swelling. You should not scratch, otherwise germs can get into the skin. Pharmacies also sell creams to stop the itching.

Some people have an **allergy** to insect venom. Then the body can react very strongly: difficulty breathing, dizziness or a rash all over the body. In this case, call the **emergency number 144** straight away. A sting in the mouth or throat is also dangerous, because the swelling can make breathing difficult. Until help arrives, the person can suck ice and you can cool the neck from the outside.

Outdoors you should cover sweet drinks and take a quick look in your glass before drinking. Wasps like sweet things and meat. If you walk barefoot in a flower meadow, you can easily step on a bee. Staying calm helps, because wild swatting tends to make wasps more aggressive.

gewusst: A honeybee usually dies after stinging a person, because its sting stays stuck.
Only female mosquitoes bite.

teile.einleitung: A paediatrician specialises in the health of children and young people. You do not only go when you are ill, but also for regular check-ups.
wichtigste: Paediatricians are experts in child and adolescent medicine.
Healthy children also go for regular check-ups.
At the check-up, height and weight are measured.
The doctor also checks eyesight, hearing and development.
You also get recommended vaccinations at the paediatrician’s.

abschnitte.text: Children are not small adults. Their bodies are constantly growing and changing. After studying medicine, **paediatricians** have done further training in **child and adolescent medicine**. They know typical childhood illnesses and know which medicines, and how much of them, are suitable for children.

Even if a child is healthy, they go for a **preventive check-up** at certain intervals. The doctor measures **height and weight** and enters them on a growth chart. This lets her see whether the child is growing well. She listens to the heart and lungs, checks the eyes and ears and asks how things are going at school and at home.

At the check-ups, the doctor also looks at the **vaccination record** and gives any missing vaccinations. Parents can ask questions about food, sleep or exercise. If necessary, the paediatrician sends the child to another expert or to the children’s hospital.

Many children are a bit nervous before a visit to the doctor. It helps to talk beforehand about what will happen. You are also allowed to ask the doctor questions yourself. The costs of the visits are usually covered by the health insurer’s **basic insurance**.

gewusst: In the first years of life, check-ups are especially frequent, because babies and toddlers develop very quickly.
Many children go to the same paediatrician until the end of compulsory schooling or even longer.

teile.einleitung: Tax remission means that the state waives all or part of a tax. This only happens when someone has got into genuine hardship and submits a request for this reason. The authority checks each case carefully.
wichtigste: With tax remission, the state waives all or part of a tax.
You have to submit a written request for it.
It requires genuine hardship, usually through no fault of your own.
The authority checks income, wealth and expenses.
Often a payment plan or a deferral of payment is already enough to help.

abschnitte.text: Sometimes someone really cannot pay their taxes, for example after a long illness, because of unemployment or after an accident. Then paying is a **severe hardship**. In such a **situation of hardship** you can submit a **request for remission**. However, remission is an exception and not a right that you simply get.

The request goes to the responsible tax authority. In it you explain why you cannot pay and enclose supporting documents. The authority checks your income, your wealth and your necessary expenses. Then it decides whether the tax is remitted **in full**, **in part** or **not at all**.

If the hardship is only temporary, there are other options. You can ask to pay in **instalments**, in other words pay the taxes in several parts. A **deferral of payment** is also possible. It is important to contact the tax office early and not simply stop paying.

gewusst: Anyone who has concealed income usually cannot get remission for those taxes.

teile.einleitung: The HMO model is a special form of basic insurance. You commit to going to a particular health centre first when you have health problems. In return you pay a lower premium.
wichtigste: HMO stands for **Health Maintenance Organization**.
The first point of contact is a **health centre** with several experts.
If necessary, the centre refers you to specialists or to hospital.
In return, the **premium** is lower than in the standard model.
In an **emergency** you may go straight to the nearest hospital.

abschnitte.text: In the **HMO model** you choose a particular **health centre**. Several doctors and often other experts work there together. Anyone who is ill always goes there first. If you need a specialist or treatment in hospital, the centre **refers** you. Without a referral, the insurer usually does not pay.

Because the health centre coordinates the treatment, there are fewer duplicate examinations. This saves costs. That is why the **premium** in the HMO model is **lower** than in the standard model with a free choice of doctor. But the services of basic insurance are exactly the same. In an **emergency** you may go straight to hospital.

As well as HMO there are other **alternative insurance models**. In the **family doctor model** you go to your own family doctor first. In the **Telmed model** you first call a telephone advice service. In the **standard model** you may freely choose which doctor you go to, but you pay the highest premium. The idea of the HMO model originally comes from the **USA**.

gewusst: In Switzerland, HMO centres are found mainly in cities and larger towns.
Like the deductible, you can change the model with effect from the start of each year.

teile.einleitung: When someone is ill, you wish them “Get well soon”. With this you are saying: I hope you will be healthy again soon. Small gestures such as a card or a phone call can make a sick person very happy.
wichtigste: You say “**Get well soon**” to someone who is ill or injured.
You are saying that you hope they will soon be healthy again.
A **card**, a drawing or a phone call can make them happy.
When **visiting someone who is ill**, you do not stay too long.
Anyone who is ill with something infectious does not visit anyone in hospital.

abschnitte.text: In German, “Gute Besserung” means that you hope the sick person will soon feel better. You say it to friends, family members or classmates who are ill in bed or have hurt themselves. Adults say it to each other too, for example at work. The wish shows: **I am thinking of you**.

Anyone who is ill often has to stay at home and gets bored. That is why they are pleased about small gestures. You can write a **card**, make a **drawing** or give them a quick **phone call**. Classmates can also bring the homework round so that you do not miss anything. Sometimes a message on the mobile phone is enough.

When **visiting someone who is ill** in hospital or at home, a few simple rules apply. Ask beforehand whether the visit is convenient. Do not stay too long, because sick people get tired quickly. Anyone who has a cold themselves or is ill with something infectious is better off staying away. And in hospital, stick to the **visiting hours**.

Several languages are spoken in Switzerland, and this wish exists in all of them. In French, for example, you say **“Bon rétablissement”**. In Italian you wish **“Buona guarigione”**. In English it is **“Get well soon”**. This way you can wish friends in other language regions a quick recovery too.

gewusst: A laugh or a cheerful visit does not replace medicine, but it can do a sick person good.
Many hospitals have their own rules about whether you may bring flowers.

teile.einleitung: State school is the compulsory schooling that all children in Switzerland attend. It includes kindergarten, primary school and lower secondary school. Because it is paid for with taxes, it is free for children.
wichtigste: State school is free for all children.
This is set out in the Federal Constitution.
The cantons and municipalities are responsible for schools.
It is paid for with tax money.
Teachers’ salaries, school buildings and materials cost a lot of money.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland all children have to go to school. In most cantons **compulsory schooling** lasts eleven years, with kindergarten, **primary school** and **lower secondary school**. The **Federal Constitution** says that basic education at state schools must be **free of charge**. This means that parents do not pay school fees.

The **cantons** are responsible for state schools. They set the curriculum, for example. The **municipalities** often build the school buildings and organise everyday school life. All this is paid for with **tax money**. Salaries for teachers, buildings, books and exercise books cost a lot of money every year.

People without children also pay taxes that go into schools. The idea behind it: a good education benefits the whole of society. Well-educated people find work and later contribute to the community themselves. For outings or school camps, parents sometimes pay a small contribution.

gewusst: With the HarmoS agreement, many cantons have brought key features of schooling into line, such as the age at which children start school.

teile.einleitung: You measure body temperature with a thermometer. That way you can find out whether someone has a fever. A thermometer belongs in every home first aid kit.
wichtigste: A **thermometer** measures body temperature.
Normal body temperature is about **37 degrees Celsius**.
From about 38 degrees, people speak of a **fever**.
Today, **digital** thermometers are mostly used.
You can measure, for example, under the armpit, in the mouth or in the ear.

abschnitte.text: When someone feels hot, you do not yet know exactly whether they have a fever. The **thermometer** shows the exact body temperature. If it is clearly above the normal value of about 37 degrees, you have a fever. The temperature is given in **degrees Celsius**.

Today most thermometers are **digital**. They beep when the measurement is finished and show the number on a small screen. **Ear thermometers** measure in a few seconds using infrared. There are also thermometers for the **forehead**. In the past, thermometers were made of glass and contained poisonous **mercury**.

You can measure in different places: under the **armpit**, in the **mouth** or in the **ear**. Depending on the place, the value is slightly different. Under the armpit, for example, it is a little lower than in the mouth. It is important to read the instructions and to clean the thermometer after use.

The temperature scale in **degrees Celsius** goes back to the Swedish scientist **Anders Celsius**. He proposed it in the 18th century. Water freezes at 0 degrees and boils at 100 degrees. In the USA, on the other hand, temperature is usually measured in **degrees Fahrenheit**. There, about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit is considered normal body temperature.

gewusst: 37 degrees Celsius is about 98.6 degrees Fahrenheit.
A good ear thermometer only needs a few seconds for a measurement.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is built like a house with three floors: municipality, canton and Confederation. The municipality is the smallest level, the Confederation the largest. Each level has its own tasks and collects its own taxes.
wichtigste: The three levels of government are municipality, canton and Confederation.
The municipality is the smallest level.
Several municipalities together lie in one canton.
All 26 cantons together form the Confederation, in other words Switzerland.
Each level has its own parliament and its own government.
What a smaller level can do itself, it should do itself.

abschnitte.text: The **municipality** is the smallest level of government and the closest to the people. There are over 2000 municipalities in Switzerland, from small mountain villages to large cities. The municipality looks after things like primary school, water, rubbish and local roads. Many municipalities have a **municipal assembly**, while larger ones have a municipal parliament.

Several municipalities form a **canton**. Switzerland has 26 cantons, for example Zurich, Bern, Ticino or the Grisons. Each canton has its own constitution, a parliament, a government and courts. Cantons are responsible for things like the police, hospitals and upper secondary schools. They also set their own taxes.

All the cantons together form the **Confederation**, in other words the Swiss Confederation. The Confederation is the largest level. It looks after tasks for the whole country, for example the army, foreign policy, national roads and the AVS. Its seat is in Bern. The Confederation may only do what the Federal Constitution allows it to do.

In Switzerland the principle of **subsidiarity** applies. This means: what the municipality can do well by itself, it does itself. Only what it cannot manage alone is taken over by the canton. And only when a task concerns the whole country is the Confederation responsible. This division is called **federalism**.

gewusst: The number of municipalities has been falling for years because many small municipalities are merging.
The youngest canton is Jura, which was created in 1979.

teile.einleitung: The **way to school** leads from home to school. So that children arrive safely, there are zebra crossings, pavements and traffic lights. The municipality or the canton pays for these with tax money.
wichtigste: For many children, the way to school is an important part of the day.
Zebra crossings, pavements and traffic lights make it safer.
The municipality is responsible for municipal roads, the canton for cantonal roads.
Their upkeep is paid for with taxes.
In Switzerland, zebra crossings are yellow.
The Swiss German rule “Warte, luege, lose, laufe” helps when crossing the road.

abschnitte.text: Many children in Switzerland go to school **on foot** or by **bike**. On the way to school they meet friends, get exercise and learn to find their way around in **traffic**. That is why experts recommend letting children go by themselves where possible. But the way should be as safe as possible.

A **zebra crossing** shows where you may cross the road. In Switzerland the stripes are **yellow**. The paint wears off over time and has to be repainted. Because the crossing is part of the road, it is paid for by the **municipality** or the **canton**, depending on who owns the road. The money comes from **taxes**.

For children there is a simple Swiss German rule: **“Warte, luege, lose, laufe”**, which means “wait, look, listen, walk”. You stop at the edge of the road, look left and right, listen for cars and only go when the vehicles have stopped. On the zebra crossing too, it is important to make eye contact with the drivers. A **reflective band** or bright clothes help you to be seen.

The **police** visit many schools and practise the right behaviour in traffic with the children. Older children often take a **cycling test**. Some municipalities use **school crossing patrols** at dangerous spots. If a way to school is too long or too dangerous, the municipality sometimes has to organise a **school bus**.

gewusst: In Switzerland, courts have already had to decide whether a way to school is reasonable.
Many municipalities create 30 km/h zones in front of school buildings so that cars drive more slowly.

teile.einleitung: Many different mushrooms grow in the woods. Some taste good, others are very poisonous and can even be deadly. That is why you never eat a mushroom that you do not know for sure.
wichtigste: Some mushrooms are very poisonous, even if they look harmless.
Many poisonous mushrooms look very similar to edible ones.
In Switzerland you can have mushrooms you have picked checked at a mushroom inspection point.
If you suspect mushroom poisoning, call Tox Info Suisse on 145.
Fungi are neither plants nor animals, but a kingdom of living things of their own.

abschnitte.text: **Fungi** are neither plants nor animals. They form their own **kingdom** of living things. What we see in the woods is only the **fruiting body**. Most of the fungus grows underground as a fine network of threads. This network is called the **mycelium**.

Some mushrooms are **very poisonous**. One of the most dangerous is the **death cap**. Even a single mushroom can be deadly for a person. Many poisonous mushrooms look very similar to edible ones. That is why the rule is: **never eat** unknown mushrooms, and do not even taste them.

In many Swiss municipalities there is a **mushroom inspection point**. There, trained experts check the mushrooms people have picked, usually free of charge. They sort out poisonous and inedible mushrooms. You bring all the mushrooms you have picked, because one poisonous mushroom can spoil the others. In some cantons there are rules on when and how many mushrooms you may pick.

If someone may have eaten a poisonous mushroom, call **Tox Info Suisse** on the number **145** straight away. If the symptoms are severe, dial **144**. Keep any leftover mushrooms so that experts can identify them. Some mushroom poisons only take effect after many hours. That is why you act quickly, even if you still feel fine.

gewusst: A honey fungus in the USA, which spreads underground over many square kilometres, is considered one of the largest living things on Earth.
Some mushroom poisons only take effect hours after eating, when the poison is already in the body.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who is ill and cannot work may not earn any money. Sickness benefit insurance then pays part of the wages. However, it is not part of compulsory basic insurance.
wichtigste: Sickness benefit replaces part of your wages when you are ill.
Basic insurance pays for treatment, but not to replace lost wages.
Sickness benefit insurance is voluntary.
Many employers take it out for their staff.
Often 80 % of the wages is paid.

abschnitte.text: A **daily allowance** is an amount of money paid for each day on which you cannot work because of illness. It is meant to partly replace **lost wages**. This means employees can still pay their rent and bills during a longer illness. The treatment itself, on the other hand, is paid for by the health insurer.

By law, an employer only has to continue paying wages during illness for a **limited time**. How long depends on how long someone has already worked for the company. To cover longer absences, many companies take out **collective sickness benefit insurance**. It often pays **80 % of the wages** for up to two years.

In Switzerland, sickness benefit insurance is **voluntary**. Whether you are insured through your employer is stated in your employment contract or in a collective labour agreement. **Self-employed people** have to take care of it themselves. Anyone who is not insured can get into financial difficulties during a longer illness.

gewusst: In the case of an accident, it is not sickness benefit insurance that pays, but for employees the compulsory accident insurance pays a daily allowance.
If someone is unable to work for a long time, the disability insurance (IV) may later become responsible.

teile.einleitung: **Saving** means not spending money unnecessarily. A municipality also has to handle its money carefully, because tax money is everyone's money. That is why a budget is planned and checked every year.
wichtigste: Tax money is money that all taxpayers raise together.
A municipality plans its spending in a budget.
The municipal assembly or the municipal parliament decides on the budget.
At the end of the year, the accounts show how much was really spent.
An auditing committee checks that everything is correct.
The Confederation has a debt brake so that it does not run up too many debts.

abschnitte.text: The municipality gets its money mainly from **taxes**. With it, it pays for schools, roads, water pipes, the fire service and much more. Because the money comes from everyone, it should also be used sensibly for everyone. **Saving** here does not mean spending nothing at all, but using the money wisely and carefully.

Every year the municipality makes a plan for its spending and income. This plan is called the **budget** or estimate. The **municipal council** proposes it. In smaller municipalities the **municipal assembly** decides, in larger ones a **municipal parliament**. There people discuss what money is needed for and where savings can be made.

At the end of the year, the **accounts** show how much was really spent. An **auditing committee** or finance committee checks whether everything was done correctly. After that, the voters or the parliament must approve the accounts. In this way it remains visible what happens to the tax money.

The Confederation must also handle money economically. In 2001 the Swiss people accepted the **debt brake** by a large majority. It requires the Confederation not to spend more than it takes in over several years. Many cantons have similar rules. How strictly savings should be made is often disputed in politics.

gewusst: In many municipalities, every voter can have their say at the municipal assembly and vote on the budget.
If a municipality needs more money, it can raise its tax rate, but this usually requires a vote.

teile.einleitung: A reference date is a particular day on which something is measured or recorded. For taxes, the most important reference date is usually 31 December. On this day, the amount of your wealth is what counts.
wichtigste: A reference date is a fixed day.
For wealth, the amount at the end of the tax period applies.
This is usually 31 December.
Bank statements at the end of the year help with filling in the forms.
If tax liability ends earlier, that day counts as the reference date.

abschnitte.text: The balance of an account changes all the time. Sometimes wages come in, sometimes something is paid. So that it is clear which amount counts, there is a **reference date**. For **wealth** in the tax return, the amount at the end of the **tax period** applies, in other words usually on **31 December**.

On the reference date you count, for example, the money in **bank accounts**, the value of **securities** such as shares, and cash too. The banks send a **year-end statement** for this. For shares, the price on the reference date applies. Debts are also recorded on this day, because you may subtract them from your wealth.

Anyone who moves abroad in the middle of the year is only liable for tax in Switzerland until then. In that case, the **end of tax liability** counts as the reference date. There are reference dates for other things too. For child deductions, for example, what usually counts is how the family is made up at the end of the year.

gewusst: There is no reference date for income: what counts is everything you have earned during the whole year.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland, 144 is the emergency number for the ambulance service. Anyone who calls gets help from experts, and if necessary an ambulance comes. The call is free.
wichtigste: 144 calls the ambulance service.
You dial it when someone is seriously injured or suddenly seriously ill.
The call is free.
On the phone you say who you are, where you are and what has happened.
The experts on the phone explain what you can do until help arrives.
Trained paramedics work in the ambulance.

abschnitte.text: You dial **144** when a person is seriously injured or suddenly seriously ill. This is the case when someone is unconscious, no longer responds or can hardly breathe. You also call in case of heavy bleeding, a serious accident or severe chest pain. If in doubt, it is better to call. The experts on the phone decide what help is needed.

Anyone who dials 144 reaches an **emergency control centre**. There, experts know exactly which questions are important. They send the right **ambulance** or, if needed, a helicopter. Until help arrives, they explain on the phone what you can do. For example, they guide you step by step through **chest compressions**.

**Paramedics** work in the ambulance. They have had long training and carry a lot of equipment. They treat the person on the spot and during the journey to hospital. In particularly serious cases, an **emergency doctor** also comes along. Basic insurance pays part of the costs of such transport.

gewusst: In some regions of Switzerland, when someone’s heart stops, trained volunteers nearby are also alerted; they are called first responders.

teile.einleitung: Withholding tax is a tax of 35 per cent on certain interest, dividends and large lottery winnings. Anyone who declares everything correctly in their tax return gets this tax back in full. Its main purpose is to prevent people from hiding money from the tax office.
wichtigste: Withholding tax is 35 per cent.
It is charged on dividends, on certain interest and on large lottery winnings.
The bank or company deducts the tax and transfers it directly to the Confederation.
Anyone who declares everything correctly gets the withholding tax back.
In Switzerland, it is reclaimed through the tax return.
The tax is meant to prevent tax evasion.
Interest on bank accounts of up to 200 francs a year is exempt from it.

abschnitte.text: **Withholding tax** is a federal tax that has existed since 1944. It is deducted at source, in other words before the money reaches the person receiving it. The rate is a high 35 per cent. For honest taxpayers, however, it is only a kind of **security deposit**, because they get the money back.

It mainly affects **dividends**, in other words shares of profit that Swiss public limited companies pay out to their shareholders. It is also deducted from interest on bonds and from larger amounts of interest on bank accounts. For lottery winnings, it applies to winnings of over one million francs. Interest on a bank account of up to 200 francs a year is spared.

abschnitte.titel: How do you get it back?
abschnitte.text: You declare all accounts, securities and earnings in the **list of securities** in your tax return. The tax office then offsets the withholding tax already paid against the taxes you owe. If it is higher than the tax bill, the rest is paid out to you. This is also where the German name “Verrechnungssteuer” comes from: the tax is **offset**.

Without this tax, people could simply keep quiet about interest and dividends. Withholding tax makes this unattractive, because anyone who keeps something quiet loses 35 per cent. So it works as an incentive to be honest. At the same time, it brings the Confederation income from people who do not declare their money correctly.

Anyone who lives abroad and receives dividends from a Swiss company also pays 35 per cent withholding tax. Thanks to **double taxation agreements**, part of it can be reclaimed, but often not all of it. The refund application then goes to the Federal Tax Administration in Bern. In this way, Switzerland makes sure that foreign investors also make a contribution.

begriffe.erklaerung: Tax of 35 per cent on interest and dividends that can be reclaimed.
Part of the profit that a company pays out to its shareholders.
Security with which you lend money to a company or the state and receive interest in return.
List of all accounts and securities in the tax return.

gewusst: At 35 per cent, Switzerland has one of the highest withholding tax rates on dividends in the world.
In Switzerland, winnings from lotteries and sports betting of up to one million francs are tax-free.
Withholding tax was introduced during the Second World War.

teile.einleitung: The tax office is the authority that calculates and collects taxes. It checks tax returns and then sends out the bill. Without the tax office, nobody would know how much they have to pay.
wichtigste: The tax office calculates how much tax someone has to pay.
It collects the tax money.
It checks the tax returns of taxpayers.
There are tax offices in municipalities and cantons.
The cantons also collect direct federal tax.
Anyone who disagrees with the decision can lodge an objection.

abschnitte.titel: What does the tax office do?
abschnitte.text: The **tax office** is an authority. It sends out the forms for the **tax return** and checks what people declare. Then it calculates how much tax someone owes. This decision is called the **tax assessment**. Finally, the tax office sends a bill and collects the money.

In Switzerland there are tax offices in the **municipalities** and a **cantonal tax administration**. The work is divided differently depending on the canton. The cantons also collect **direct federal tax** and pass it on to the Confederation. For VAT, on the other hand, the **Federal Tax Administration** in Bern is responsible.

If something is unclear, the tax office can ask for documents, for example a salary statement. Anyone who thinks the assessment is wrong can lodge an **objection**. There is a deadline for this, usually 30 days. Many tax offices also help with filling in the forms and answer questions on the phone or at the counter.

gewusst: Today, in most cantons, you can fill in your tax return on the computer and submit it electronically.
Tax office staff are bound by tax secrecy and are not allowed to tell anyone anything.

teile.einleitung: The tax period is the period of time for which taxes are calculated. In Switzerland this is usually a calendar year from January to December. You fill in the tax return for it in the following year.
wichtigste: The tax period is usually a calendar year.
It runs from 1 January to 31 December.
You fill in the tax return in the following year.
So in spring 2026 you declare the year 2025.
For wealth, what counts is the amount at the end of the tax period.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland the **tax period** is the **calendar year**. Everything you earn from January to December counts as income for that period. Wealth is valued at the end of the period, usually on **31 December**. If tax liability starts or ends in the middle of the year, for example when someone moves abroad, the period is shorter.

Only when the year is over do you know exactly how much you have earned. That is why you fill in the **tax return** in the **following year**. Anyone who worked in 2025 declares this income in spring 2026. In many cantons the tax return has to be submitted by the end of March, and an extension is usually possible.

This is called **current-year assessment**: the income taxed is that of the same year for which the tax is owed. During the year, many cantons already send out a **provisional bill**. After the tax return comes the **final statement**. Any money paid in excess is refunded.

gewusst: In the past, many cantons taxed two years together, but today the single calendar year applies in all cantons.

teile.einleitung: An emergency is a situation in which someone needs help immediately. Then you call the right emergency number or go to the emergency department at the hospital. It is important to stay calm and act quickly.
wichtigste: In an emergency, someone needs help immediately.
If a person no longer responds, call 144 straight away.
144 is the number for the ambulance, 117 for the police, 118 for the fire brigade.
You can reach Rega on the number 1414.
The hospital emergency department is open day and night.
For small problems, the family doctor’s surgery or the pharmacy can often help.

abschnitte.text: An **emergency** is when a person needs help immediately. This is the case, for example, when someone is unconscious, no longer responds, can hardly breathe or is bleeding heavily. A serious accident or severe chest pain is also an emergency. Then every minute counts. Call **144** straight away.

In Switzerland there are several **emergency numbers**. **144** calls the ambulance service. **117** is the police, **118** the fire brigade and **1414** Rega. In case of poisoning, Tox Info Suisse helps on the number **145**. All these numbers are free.

The hospital has an **emergency department**. It is open day and night, including at weekends. There, experts first check who needs help most urgently. This is called **triage**. That is why people who are not so seriously ill sometimes have to wait a long time.

abschnitte.titel: Not every problem is an emergency
abschnitte.text: With a mild cold or a small graze, you do not need to go to A&E. Then the **family doctor’s surgery** or the **pharmacy** can help. Outside surgery hours, many regions have an **emergency doctor service** with its own phone number. That way the emergency department stays free for serious cases. But if in doubt, it is better to call once too often than once too rarely.

gewusst: The experts on the phone at 144 can explain how to help a person until the ambulance arrives.
In the emergency department, it is not whoever arrives first who is seen first, but whoever needs help most urgently.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who wants to take out supplementary insurance with a health insurer often has to fill in a health questionnaire. With it, the insurer wants to know how healthy you are. Then it decides whether to accept you and on what terms.
wichtigste: The **health questionnaire** is part of the application for **supplementary insurance**.
It asks about illnesses, accidents and treatments.
The insurer may **turn down** an application for supplementary insurance.
It can also make a **reservation**, in which case a particular illness is not insured.
There is no health questionnaire in **basic insurance**.

abschnitte.text: In the **health questionnaire** you answer questions about your own health. For example: have you had any illnesses, accidents or operations in recent years? Do you take medicines regularly? Are you having treatment? For children, the **parents** fill in the questionnaire. You answer all the questions fully and honestly.

Supplementary insurance is **voluntary**. Different rules apply to it than to basic insurance, namely the **Insurance Contract Act**. That is why the insurer may decide for itself whom it accepts. With the questionnaire it estimates how high the costs for a new customer could be. It can accept the application, turn it down or make a **reservation**.

In **basic insurance** things are completely different. There the **obligation to accept** applies: every insurer must accept everyone, no matter how old or how healthy they are. That is why there are no health questions there. Many parents take out supplementary insurance for their children early on, while the children are still healthy.

gewusst: Anyone who keeps an illness quiet in the questionnaire risks the insurance cancelling the contract.
You sign the questionnaire. In doing so you confirm that all the information is correct.

teile.einleitung: Value added tax, VAT for short, is a tax on almost everything you buy. Companies collect it for the state. The input tax deduction makes sure that only the added value is taxed.
wichtigste: A company owes VAT on its sales.
The VAT it has paid on its purchases is called input tax.
It may deduct the input tax from what it owes.
In this way, only the added value is taxed at each stage.
In the end, the customers bear the tax.

abschnitte.text: **Value added tax** is a federal tax. It is included in the price of almost all goods and services. Since 2024 the standard rate in Switzerland has been 8.1 per cent, and a lower rate applies to food. Companies collect the tax and pass it on to the **Federal Tax Administration**.

A bakery buys flour and pays VAT to the mill. This tax is called **input tax**. When the bakery sells bread, it charges VAT to its customers itself. When it settles its accounts, it subtracts the input tax it has paid from what it owes, and this is the **input tax deduction**. In this way it only pays tax on the **added value** that it has created itself.

At each stage, only the newly created value is taxed. The tax is passed on from stage to stage like this. In the end, the **customers** who buy the bread pay the whole tax. Private individuals cannot deduct input tax.

gewusst: Small companies with a low turnover are exempt from VAT and therefore cannot deduct input tax either.

teile.einleitung: Nurses look after people who are ill, injured or old. In hospital they are there day and night. Their job is demanding and very important for our health system.
wichtigste: Nurses look after sick people in hospital day and night.
They give medicines, dress wounds and watch how patients are doing.
They work closely with doctors.
They work in shifts, including at night and at weekends.
In Switzerland, you learn the profession at a college of higher education or a university of applied sciences.
Nurses also work in care homes and for Spitex.

abschnitte.text: **Nurses** help sick people in everyday life. They give **medicines**, dress wounds and measure temperature and blood pressure. They help with washing, eating or getting up. They watch closely how the patients are doing. If they notice that something is wrong, they call the doctor straight away.

Sick people need help at night too. That is why nurses work in **shifts**. There are early shifts, late shifts and night shifts, including at weekends and on public holidays. At every handover, they tell the next shift what is important. That way there is always someone there who knows what is going on.

Anyone who wants to become a nurse trains at a **college of higher education** or studies at a **university of applied sciences**. A common route begins with an apprenticeship as a **healthcare assistant**, FaGe for short. After that you can do further training, for example for intensive care or the emergency department. Nurses also work in old people’s homes and care homes or for **Spitex**, which looks after people at home.

Switzerland needs a lot of nurses. In 2021, voters approved the **nursing initiative**. It aims to promote training and improve working conditions in nursing. Since then, the Confederation and the cantons have been putting it into practice step by step.

gewusst: International Nurses Day is on 12 May, Florence Nightingale’s birthday.
Florence Nightingale nursed wounded soldiers in the 19th century and is regarded as the founder of modern nursing.

teile.einleitung: The **spirits tax** is a federal tax on schnapps and other distilled drinks. It is much higher than the tax on beer. A large part of the money goes to the AVS and the IV.
wichtigste: Spirits are distilled drinks such as schnapps, vodka or whisky.
The Confederation charges a spirits tax on them.
It is much higher than beer tax.
In Switzerland, wine is not charged with an alcohol tax.
A large part of the revenue goes to the AVS and the IV.
Part goes to the cantons for the fight against addiction problems.

abschnitte.text: **Spirits**, or **distilled drinks**, are drinks with a lot of alcohol. They are made by **distilling**. In this process a fermented drink is heated so that the alcohol separates out. Well-known examples are kirsch, Williams pear brandy, vodka or whisky. In Switzerland, distilling schnapps from fruit has a long tradition.

The **spirits tax** is charged by the **Confederation**. The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security is responsible for it. The tax is calculated according to the amount of **pure alcohol**. It is 29 francs per litre of pure alcohol. That is why it is much higher than **beer tax**. In Switzerland, wine is exempt from alcohol tax.

The tax is not only meant to bring in money. It is also meant to slow down the **consumption** of strong alcohol, because too much of it harms **health**. That is why the tax is so high. A large part of the revenue goes to the **AVS** and the **IV**. The cantons receive ten per cent, the so-called **alcohol tenth**. They use it against addiction problems.

In Switzerland there are age limits for alcohol. **Beer and wine** may only be sold from the age of **16**. **Spirits** are only available from the age of **18**. This also applies to mixed drinks containing spirits. Shops and restaurants must check people's age. This is meant to protect children and young people.

gewusst: In Switzerland there is a particularly high special tax on sweet mixed drinks containing spirits, known as alcopops.
In the past, the Swiss Alcohol Board supervised spirits; today this task has been incorporated into the federal customs administration.

teile.einleitung: Nosebleeds are common in children and often look worse than they are. With a few simple steps, they usually stop again after a few minutes.
wichtigste: With a nosebleed, tilt your head slightly forwards.
Squeeze the soft part of the nose shut for a few minutes.
Do not tilt your head back, otherwise blood runs into your throat.
A cool cloth on the back of the neck can help.
If it does not stop, get medical help.

abschnitte.text: At the front of the nose there are many fine **blood vessels** just under the mucous membrane. They can easily be injured, for example by blowing your nose, picking your nose, a knock or dry air in winter. Usually a nosebleed is **harmless**, even if it looks like a lot of blood.

Sit down and tilt your **head slightly forwards**. That way the blood does not run into your throat, which can make you feel sick. Then squeeze the **soft part of the nose** together with your thumb and index finger. Hold it like this for **a few minutes** without checking in between. Keep breathing calmly through your mouth.

A **cool, wet cloth** on the back of the neck can help the blood vessels contract. But do **not tilt your head back**. After a nosebleed, you should not blow your nose hard for a while. Otherwise the spot that has just closed can open up again.

abschnitte.titel: When to go to the doctor?
abschnitte.text: If the bleeding has not stopped after about **20 minutes**, get medical help. Also go to the doctor after a hard blow to the nose or head. Anyone who has nosebleeds very often should also have this checked.

gewusst: The spot at the front of the nose where bleeding happens most often has its own name in medicine: Locus Kiesselbachi.
Dry air from the heating in winter makes the lining of the nose sensitive, which is why nosebleeds are more common then.

teile.einleitung: Anyone who is ill cannot go to work or sometimes cannot go to school. With a doctor’s certificate, a doctor confirms that someone was ill. For adults it is often important for their employer.
wichtigste: A doctor’s certificate is a confirmation from the doctor that you were ill.
It states how long someone was unable to work or go to school.
The illness itself usually does not have to be stated in it.
Many employers require a certificate from the third or fourth day of illness.
A false doctor’s certificate is forbidden.

abschnitte.text: A **doctor’s certificate** is a document on which a doctor confirms that someone was ill. Above all, it states **from when to when** the person was unable to work or go to school. It often also states whether they were fully or only partly **unfit for work**, for example 50 per cent. Because of **medical confidentiality**, the exact illness is usually not stated.

Anyone who is ill must let their **employer** know straight away. In many companies you need a doctor’s certificate from the third or fourth day of illness. This is usually set out in the **employment contract** or in a set of rules. Some employers require it from the very first day. With the certificate you are entitled to have your **wages** paid for a certain time.

If children miss school because of illness, the **parents** usually excuse them to the teacher. A doctor’s certificate is usually only needed for longer absences or in special cases, for example for missed exams. The rules vary depending on the canton and the school. For apprentices, the rules of the training company often apply.

gewusst: In Switzerland, forging a doctor’s certificate or issuing one without good reason is a criminal offence.
The surgery may charge a small fee for a doctor’s certificate.
